findings.reason: install.ts:121 does `join(tmpdir(), 'spm', skillset.name)` and fetch-skillset.ts:12-14 only checks that name is a string. A name of '../../home/user' therefore resolves outside the temp folder. safePath (install.ts:82-90) checks paths against that already-escaped base, so writeFile at install.ts:130 writes under the attacker-chosen directory.
findings.claim: The temp directory is built from the remote manifest's unchecked `name`, so a malicious skillset can make install write files anywhere the user can write.
findings.evidence: `const tmpDir = join(tmpdir(), 'spm', skillset.name)`. `skillset.name` comes from `fetchSkillset`/`validateSkillset`, which only check that it is a string. `join` resolves `..`, so `name: "../../../../../../../../home/victim"` points tmpDir outside the temp folder. `safePath(tmpDir, result.path)` then checks paths against that already-escaped base, so it allows writes such as a `setup: ../../.bashrc` entry (path `claude/fsd/../../.bashrc`, which normalizes to `.bashrc`) to land at `/home/victim/.bashrc` through `writeFile`.

findings.claim: safePath uses a plain string-prefix check, so a path can escape into a sibling directory whose name starts with the base name.
